[Global Human Resources & Total Rewards Committee, Enterprise Operations | Company Global Overtime and Bonus Policy 2024 | General Overview]
# Enterprise Standard Operating Procedure: Overtime & Bonus Compensation Policy

**Document ID**: `COMPANY_OVERTIME_BONUS_POLICY_2024`  
**Issuing Authority**: Global Human Resources & Total Rewards Committee, Enterprise Operations  
**Authority Tier**: Tier 2 — Organizational Policy  
**Jurisdiction**: INDIA (All Enterprise Locations)  
**Topic**: OVERTIME, BONUS  
**Effective Date**: 2024-01-01 to CURRENT  
**Document Version**: `v1.2`

---

[Global Human Resources & Total Rewards Committee, Enterprise Operations | Company Global Overtime and Bonus Policy 2024 | 1. Eligibility for Overtime]
- Only non-exempt operational staff, technical support engineers, and customer operations specialists at `Intern`, `Junior`, or `Mid-level` designations are eligible for overtime compensation.
- Employees at `Senior`, `Manager`, or `Director` levels are exempt from overtime and receive fixed managerial salaries.

[Global Human Resources & Total Rewards Committee, Enterprise Operations | Company Global Overtime and Bonus Policy 2024 | 2. Overtime Rate Calculation Formula]
Overtime hours approved in the biometric attendance system shall be compensated at **1.5x (one and a half times) the standard hourly basic wage rate**:
$$\text{Hourly Basic Rate} = \frac{\text{Basic Salary}}{\text{Working Days (26)} \times \text{Daily Hours (8)}}$$
$$\text{Overtime Payout} = \text{Overtime Hours} \times \text{Hourly Basic Rate} \times 1.50$$

[Global Human Resources & Total Rewards Committee, Enterprise Operations | Company Global Overtime and Bonus Policy 2024 | 3. Monthly Overtime Cap]
- Maximum permissible overtime without special authorization is **40 hours per month**.
- Logging overtime in excess of **60 hours per month** triggers an automated operational compliance audit flag (`EXCESSIVE_OVERTIME`).

---

[Global Human Resources & Total Rewards Committee, Enterprise Operations | Company Global Overtime and Bonus Policy 2024 | 1. Festive Diwali Bonus (October Cycle)]
All active employees completed probation as of 30th September are eligible for a discretionary festive Diwali bonus ranging from ₹15,000 to ₹60,000 based on employee band.

[Global Human Resources & Total Rewards Committee, Enterprise Operations | Company Global Overtime and Bonus Policy 2024 | 2. Annual Performance Appraisal Bonus (March Cycle)]
Performance bonuses disbursed during the March annual appraisal cycle range from 8% to 25% of annual basic salary based on verified performance appraisal rating (Exceeds Expectations / Outstanding).

[Global Human Resources & Total Rewards Committee, Enterprise Operations | Company Global Overtime and Bonus Policy 2024 | 3. Out-of-Cycle Discretionary Bonuses]
Any ad-hoc bonus exceeding ₹100,000 outside the standard March/October appraisal cycles requires dual authorization from the Chief Financial Officer and VP of People Operations.

[Human Resources Department, Enterprise Operations | Company Leave and Attendance Policy 2024 | General Overview]
# Enterprise Leave, Attendance & Loss of Pay (LOP) Policy

**Document ID**: `COMPANY_LEAVE_ATTENDANCE_POLICY_2024`  
**Issuing Authority**: Human Resources Department, Enterprise Operations  
**Authority Tier**: Tier 2 — Organizational Policy  
**Jurisdiction**: INDIA (All Enterprise Locations)  
**Topic**: LEAVE, WAGES  
**Effective Date**: 2024-01-01 to CURRENT  
**Document Version**: `v1.0`

---

[Human Resources Department, Enterprise Operations | Company Leave and Attendance Policy 2024 | 1. Monthly Working Days Definition]
- The standard payroll calculation month is configured based on **26 calendar working days** (excluding weekly off days).
- In any single calendar month, the sum of `present_days + leave_days` must strictly satisfy:
$$\text{present\_days} + \text{leave\_days} \le \text{working\_days}$$
- Recording `present_days > working_days` (e.g. 32 days present in a 26-day month) constitutes a mathematical impossibility and must be flagged immediately as `IMPOSSIBLE_ATTENDANCE`.

---

[Human Resources Department, Enterprise Operations | Company Leave and Attendance Policy 2024 | 1. Gross Salary Formula]
Monthly gross salary must reconcile exactly to:
$$\text{gross\_salary} = \text{basic\_salary} + \text{allowances} + \text{overtime\_amount} + \text{bonus}$$
Any discrepancy where gross does not equal the arithmetic sum constitutes `RULE_GROSS_RECONCILIATION_FAIL`.

[Human Resources Department, Enterprise Operations | Company Leave and Attendance Policy 2024 | 2. Net Take-Home Salary Formula]
Net salary disbursed to employee bank accounts must reconcile to:
$$\text{net\_salary} = \text{gross\_salary} - \text{total\_deductions}$$
$$\text{total\_deductions} = \text{pf} + \text{esi} + \text{tds} + \text{other\_deductions}$$
Any arithmetic mismatch constitutes `ABNORMAL_NET_SALARY`.

[Human Resources Department, Enterprise Operations | Company Leave and Attendance Policy 2024 | 3. Loss of Pay (LOP) Deduction Calculation]
When an employee takes unauthorized unapproved leaves, per-day salary is deducted proportionally:
$$\text{Daily Wage Rate} = \frac{\text{Gross Monthly Salary}}{\text{Working Days (26)}}$$
$$\text{LOP Deduction} = \text{Unapproved Absent Days} \times \text{Daily Wage Rate}$$

[Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India | EPFO Employees Provident Funds Act 1952 | General Overview]
# Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

**Document ID**: `EPFO_ACT_1952`  
**Issuing Authority**: Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India  
**Authority Tier**: Tier 1 — Authoritative Government Regulation  
**Jurisdiction**: INDIA (All States)  
**Topic**: PF (Provident Fund)  
**Effective Date**: 1952-11-01 to CURRENT  
**Document Version**: `v2.4`

---

[Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India | EPFO Employees Provident Funds Act 1952 | 1. Mandatory Statutory Contribution Rates]
The contribution which shall be paid by the employer to the Provident Fund shall be **12% of the basic wages, dearness allowance, and retaining allowance** (if any) for the time being payable to each of the employees (whether employed directly by such employer or by or through a contractor).

The employee's contribution shall be equal to the contribution payable by the employer in respect of him:
- **Employee Contribution**: 12.0% of Basic Salary + DA
- **Employer Contribution**: 12.0% of Basic Salary + DA

[Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India | EPFO Employees Provident Funds Act 1952 | 2. Breakdown of Employer's Statutory Contribution]
The employer's 12% contribution is split as follows:
- **3.67%** credited directly to the employee's **Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) Account**.
- **8.33%** credited to the **Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS)**, subject to the statutory wage ceiling.

[Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India | EPFO Employees Provident Funds Act 1952 | 3. Statutory Wage Ceiling Threshold]
The statutory wage ceiling for mandatory EPF coverage is **₹15,000 per month**. 
- For employees earning a basic wage up to ₹15,000 per month, contribution at 12% is mandatory.
- For employees earning basic wages exceeding ₹15,000 per month, the employer and employee may mutually agree to contribute either on the statutory ceiling of ₹15,000 (i.e. ₹1,800/month) or on the actual higher basic salary.
- In modern enterprise software practice, standard deduction is calculated as `0.12 * basic_salary`. Any deviation exceeding rounding tolerances constitutes a statutory calculation error.

[Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India | EPFO Employees Provident Funds Act 1952 | 4. Administrative and EDLI Charges]
In addition to the 12% contribution:
- **EPF Administrative Charges (Account 2)**: 0.50% of basic wages.
- **Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI) Contribution (Account 21)**: 0.50% of basic wages (capped at ₹15,000 wage ceiling = max ₹75/month).

[Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India | EPFO Employees Provident Funds Act 1952 | 5. Penalty for Non-Compliance and Default]
Under Section 14 of the Act, failure to deposit provident fund contributions within 15 days of the close of the month attracts statutory damages under Section 14B ranging from 5% to 25% per annum alongside penal interest under Section 7Q at 12% per annum.

[Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India | ESIC Employees State Insurance Act 1948 | General Overview]
# Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 & Gazette Notification S.O. 2026(E)

**Document ID**: `ESIC_ACT_1948`  
**Issuing Authority**: Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India  
**Authority Tier**: Tier 1 — Authoritative Government Regulation  
**Jurisdiction**: INDIA (All Implemented Areas)  
**Topic**: ESI (Employees State Insurance)  
**Effective Date**: 2019-07-01 to CURRENT  
**Document Version**: `v3.1`

---

[Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India | ESIC Employees State Insurance Act 1948 | 1. Monthly Wage Ceiling Limit]
Under Rule 50 of the ESI (Central) Rules, 1950 (as amended), an employee whose **gross monthly wages (excluding overtime remuneration)** do not exceed **₹21,000 per month** is mandatorily coverable under the ESI Scheme.
- For employees with certified disabilities (under Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016), the statutory wage ceiling is **₹25,000 per month**.
- **Ineligible Employees**: Any employee whose regular gross monthly wages exceed ₹21,000.00 is strictly **exempt from ESI deduction**. Deducting ESI from an ineligible employee constitutes an erroneous payroll deduction.

[Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India | ESIC Employees State Insurance Act 1948 | 2. Statutory Contribution Rates (Effective from 1st July 2019)]
Vide Ministry of Labour and Employment Gazette Notification No. S.O. 2026(E) dated 13th June 2019, the reduced statutory contribution rates are:
- **Employee Share**: **0.75%** of gross monthly wages.
- **Employer Share**: **3.25%** of gross monthly wages.
- **Total Combined Contribution**: **4.00%** of gross monthly wages.

[Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India | ESIC Employees State Insurance Act 1948 | 3. Computation Base for ESI]
The computation of ESI must include:
- Basic salary
- Dearness Allowance (DA)
- House Rent Allowance (HRA)
- Conveyance, city compensatory, and special allowances
- Production/attendance incentives paid in the monthly pay cycle

*Exclusions*: Annual bonus, ex-gratia payments, gratuity, and retrenchment compensation are excluded from gross wages for ESI computation.

[Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India | ESIC Employees State Insurance Act 1948 | 4. Mid-Period Wage Hike Continuity Rule]
If the monthly gross wages of an employee exceed ₹21,000 after the start of a contribution period (April–September or October–March), the employee continues to be covered and deductions must continue until the end of that statutory contribution period.

[Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Ministry of Finance, Government of India | Income Tax Act 1961 Section 192 TDS | General Overview]
# Income-tax Act, 1961 — Section 192 (Salary TDS)

**Document ID**: `INCOME_TAX_SEC_192`  
**Issuing Authority**: Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Ministry of Finance, Government of India  
**Authority Tier**: Tier 1 — Authoritative Government Regulation  
**Jurisdiction**: INDIA (All States)  
**Topic**: TDS (Tax Deducted at Source)  
**Effective Date**: 2023-04-01 to CURRENT  
**Document Version**: `v4.0`

---

[Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Ministry of Finance, Government of India | Income Tax Act 1961 Section 192 TDS | 1. Statutory Employer Obligation]
Any person responsible for paying any income chargeable under the head "Salaries" shall, at the time of payment, deduct income-tax on the amount payable at the **average rate of income-tax computed on the basis of the rates in force for the financial year** in which the payment is made, on the estimated income of the assessee under this head for that financial year.

[Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Ministry of Finance, Government of India | Income Tax Act 1961 Section 192 TDS | 2. Method of Monthly TDS Computation]
The employer must:
1. Estimate the employee's total gross annual salary earnings across the entire 12-month financial year (April to March), including basic, allowances, regular bonuses, and overtime projections.
2. Deduct statutory standard deduction of **₹50,000** (under Section 16(ia)).
3. Apply declared tax regime (Default New Tax Regime under Section 115BAC or Old Tax Regime).
4. Calculate net total annual tax liability including 4% Health & Education Cess.
5. Divide net annual tax liability equally across the remaining payroll months of the financial year to determine the monthly TDS deduction amount.

[Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Ministry of Finance, Government of India | Income Tax Act 1961 Section 192 TDS | 3. Adjustment for Bonuses and Increment Arrears]
When an employee receives a one-time performance bonus or salary revision increment, the employer is statutory required to recalculate the estimated annual taxable income and adjust the monthly TDS deduction proportionately for the remaining months of the financial year to prevent year-end tax deficit.

[Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Ministry of Finance, Government of India | Income Tax Act 1961 Section 192 TDS | 4. Non-Deduction and Default Penalties]
Under Section 201(1A), failure to deduct or deposit TDS attracts mandatory interest at **1.5% per month** from the date on which tax was deductible to the date of actual payment into the government treasury.

[Commercial Taxes Department, Government of Karnataka | Karnataka Tax on Professions Act 1976 | 1. Statutory Deduction Slabs]
Under Section 3 and the Schedule to the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976 (as amended by Karnataka Act No. 14 of 2023):

| Monthly Gross Salary Range | Statutory Monthly Tax Payable |
| :--- | :---: |
| **Less than ₹15,000.00** | **₹0.00 (Nil - Exempt)** |
| **₹15,000.00 and Above** | **₹200.00 per month** |

[Commercial Taxes Department, Government of Karnataka | Karnataka Tax on Professions Act 1976 | 2. Annual Limit and Exemption Threshold]
- The exemption threshold for salaried employees in Karnataka was officially raised from ₹10,000 to **₹15,000 per month** effective 1st April 2023.
- For all employees with gross earnings $\ge ₹15,000$, a uniform flat deduction of **₹200.00 per month** (₹2,400.00 annually) is statutory mandated.
- Any deduction exceeding ₹200/month or deducting Professional Tax from an employee earning $< ₹15,000$ in Karnataka is non-compliant.

[Commercial Taxes Department, Government of Karnataka | Karnataka Tax on Professions Act 1976 | 3. Senior Citizen Exemption]
Employees aged 60 years and above are fully exempt from Professional Tax in the state of Karnataka.

Under Section 3 and Schedule I of the Maharashtra State Tax on Professions Act, 1975 (as amended by Maharashtra Finance Act, 2023):

[Department of Goods and Services Tax, Government of Maharashtra | Maharashtra State Professional Tax Act 1975 | 1. Monthly Deduction Slabs for Salaried Employees in Maharashtra]
| Monthly Gross Salary Range | Monthly Tax for Male Employees | Monthly Tax for Female Employees |

[Department of Goods and Services Tax, Government of Maharashtra | Maharashtra State Professional Tax Act 1975 | 2. February Surcharge Adjustment Rule]
To ensure the annual total deduction equals exactly the statutory maximum cap of **₹2,500.00 per annum**:
- For months March to January (11 months): **₹200.00 per month** ($11 \times 200 = ₹2,200$)
- For the month of February (1 month): **₹300.00**
- Total Annual Tax = $2,200 + 300 = \text{₹2,500.00}$.

[Department of Goods and Services Tax, Government of Maharashtra | Maharashtra State Professional Tax Act 1975 | 3. Exemption for Female Employees]
Vide 2023 amendment, women earning monthly gross salary up to **₹25,000.00** are completely exempt from Professional Tax in Maharashtra state.
